name: Question 20
problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]},\,C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]},\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given above. Find $[x]_{C}.$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ relative to the basis $C.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -6 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 7 \\ 5 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 7 \\ 5 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

B={[−10],[1−1]},C={[15],[16]},[x]B=[12]

The bases B and C of R2 and the coordinates of the vector x relative to the basis B are given above. Find [x]C.

a
[2−6]
b
[8−7]
c
[52]
d
[−17]
e
[1−8]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B and C as {b1,b2} and {c1,c2}, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of B relative to the basis C.

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of b1 and b2 relative to the basis C. We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix M=[||||c1c2b1b2||||].

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination

M=[11−11560−1]R2:=R2+(−5)R1∼[11−11015−6]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[10−67015−6]

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix PB→C is

PB→C=[−675−6].

Finally, we compute [x]C:

[x]C=PB→C[x]B=[−675−6][12]=[8−7]
